artworks.title: Prowess of Deiphobus
artworks.description: Miniature from the Histoire ancienne jusqu'à César (British Library, Royal MS 20 D I, f. 126r). Deiphobus rides in armed prowess among the Trojan knights — Priam's son as a medieval chivalric hero before the sack that, in Virgil, leaves him mutilated in the underworld.

artworks.title: Cassandra Preventing Deiphobus from Killing Paris
artworks.description: Drawing by Jean Cousin in the Metropolitan Museum of Art. Cassandra restrains Deiphobus as he raises a weapon against Paris — the brother who later inherits Helen after Paris' death, here still the rival who would have ended the war by ending the abductor.

artworks.title: Paris Attacked by Deiphobus
artworks.description: Etruscan alabaster cinerary urn in the Museo Guarnacci, Volterra. Deiphobus assaults Paris while Aphrodite, Hector, Hecuba and Priam look on — the recognition scene in which the herdsman-prince is attacked by his own brother before the house of Troy claims him.

artworks.title: Recognition of Paris Attacked by Deiphobus
artworks.description: Etruscan alabaster funerary urn in the Museo archeologico nazionale di Chiusi. The relief shows Paris under attack by Deiphobus at the moment of recognition — the same fraternal assault the Volterra workshops carved for tombs across Etruria.

popCulture.title: Deiphobus
popCulture.description: Helen's last Trojan husband endures as the brother Odysseus and Menelaus butcher in the sack — Priam's son who inherited Paris's prize.
